correctness.rationale: For 0<K<1 and b1>b2, direct equilibrium balances force the listed unique interior coordinates. On the invariant product of simplices, differentiation gives the displayed 4x4 Jacobian. Its determinant is epsilon^2 d B t(a-c)>0. The exact Schur-complement eigenvalue identity and the bounds Re(1/lambda)>=0, Re[1/(lambda+epsilon t)]>=0, and 0<=Re[1/(lambda+a)]<=1/a, combined with f+d(cB-aA)/a^2>0, exclude every eigenvalue with nonnegative real part at every epsilon>0. The two off-simplex modes are -mu1 and -epsilon mu2. The key positivity follows from strict physical feasibility and K<1. Exact symbolic checks replay the full and reduced Jacobians and an admissible rational example. The degenerate K=0,b1=b2 neutral-continuum case is explicitly excluded.

value.rationale: The original six-compartment slow–fast epidemiological study left the four-dimensional interior spectral classification unresolved except by an example. The present theorem resolves whether finite information/epidemic time-scale ratios can cause local Hopf loss at fully mixed coexistence and provides sharp existence inequalities. This is a structural all-parameter stability result for the studied interaction mechanism, not a routine special numerical parameter check. It does not claim global attraction or rule out global periodic dynamics.
